Hi Sofia / Evan —

Thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap from our demo and an initial model shortlist with rationale so you have something concrete to share with the BrightLane team. I kept this focused on the three options we touched on during the call and mapped them to the tradeoffs you care about (cost, latency, quality / hallucination risk).

Executive summary (recommended order):
1) RW-Instruct-7B-quant (cost-first)
   - Why: ~good extraction and consistent structured outputs for the search/qa flows you described, lowest unit cost.
   - Benchmarks (internal subset): p95 latency ~120ms (single-request, 16-token output), hallucination rate ~6% (measured on our prompt set), cost estimate ~$0.45 / 1k generated tokens.
   - When to pick: if BrightLane prioritizes throughput and minimizing inference spend for customer-facing search.

2) Llama-3-13B-opt (balanced)
   - Why: stronger open-domain reasoning and fewer hallucinations vs smaller quantized models, while staying below the high-end model cost.
   - Benchmarks: p95 latency ~220ms, hallucination rate ~3.2% on our eval prompts, cost estimate ~$1.20 / 1k tokens.
   - When to pick: if you need better quality on long-tail queries without the highest cost.

3) Falcon-40B-raw (highest-quality / long-context)
   - Why: best on complex summarization/aggregation tasks and long contexts; highest compute cost.
   - Benchmarks: p95 latency ~520ms (long context config), hallucination rate ~1.1% on extractive QA, cost estimate ~$3.60 / 1k tokens.
   - When to pick: if accuracy on nuanced summaries is the top priority and cost/latency are acceptable for that route.

Notes on our methodology:
- Benchmarks above are from a 10k-example eval subset (attached CSV) using your demo prompts plus additional prompt variations (attached prompt-set-v1.txt).
- Hallucination rate is measured as the percent of model outputs that contain at least one confidently assertive false statement vs. ground truth annotations.
- Latency measured p95 on Redwood Hosted with the batching policy we discussed (max batch=8, async tail latency optimizations enabled).

Quality-regression risk: our quantized 7B model can occasionally drop in factual precision on nested reasoning / multi-hop extraction examples — we flagged ~4 examples / 1k where the 7B variant switched a numeric entity or date. Llama-3-13B reduces those by ~55% in our tests.

Suggested next steps (pick one):
- Short POC (recommended): 7-day eval on a 2k-item subset (we'll run the three models and produce per-prompt diffs + cost projections).
- Pilot (quality-first): run an A/B canary with Llama-3-13B vs current baseline on 5% of production queries for two weeks. Redwood will provide monitoring hooks + automatic fallback to RW-Instruct-7B-quant if latency or error rates exceed thresholds.

If useful I can kick off the 7-day eval today — we only need a short confirmation of the evaluation cohort and a signed minimal SOW (link below) to get provisioning.

Links: HubSpot deal, Drive eval folder, minimal SOW: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/BL-2026-153 | https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-demo-evals | https://redwood-inference.app/sow/BL-2026-153

Attachments: benchmark-summary-20260310.csv, prompt-set-v1.txt

Thanks — looking forward to your preference.

Hi Sofia / Evan —

Quick answers + attachments (benchmark-summary-20260310.csv attached):

1) Example failure cases (from prompt-set-v1.txt):
   - prompt ID p_0421: multi-field extraction from a nested policy doc. RW-Instruct-7B-quant swapped two date fields; Llama-3-13B returns correct pairs 98% of the time.
   - prompt ID p_1134: multi-sentence aggregation where the model must reconcile conflicting facts across paragraphs; 7B hallucinated an unsupported claim in ~7% of samples, Llama-3-13B at 1.5%.

2) Pricing: the per-1k-token numbers Alex listed are raw inference cost estimates. Final Redwood invoice would add platform/serving fees — for this deal our proposal uses a blended multiplier of 1.25x on raw inference (so $0.45 -> $0.56 / 1k for RW-Instruct-7B-quant). I'll have finance produce the exact line items in the SOW draft (SLA-exceptions-draft.docx attached).

3) Automatic fallback triggers (recommended canary policy):
   - Latency: p95 > 350ms for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows
   - Error rate: 5xx responses > 0.5% over a 10-minute window
   - Quality signal: custom checkpoint where our evaluation hook detects hallucination-rate delta > 2% vs baseline on a rolling sample of 500 queries
   - If any trigger occurs, traffic is automatically routed to RW-Instruct-7B-quant for up to 60 minutes while ops investigate.

4) Provisioning time: 2–4 hours to provision endpoints in the us-west region for the 7-day eval (we pre-warm GPU pool and deploy model variants).

Baseline numbers (full CSV in attachment):
- RW-Instruct-7B-quant: p50 48ms, p95 120ms, avg cost $0.45/1k tokens, hallucination-rate 6.0%
- Llama-3-13B-opt: p50 92ms, p95 220ms, avg cost $1.20/1k tokens, hallucination-rate 3.2%
- Falcon-40B-raw: p50 210ms, p95 520ms, avg cost $3.60/1k tokens, hallucination-rate 1.1%

Caveats: quantization and aggressive batching can reduce cost further for the 7B option but may raise hallucination on very precise extraction tasks. We included prompt-level diffs in the CSV so you can see which prompts move between labels.

Happy to hop on a 20-minute follow-up if you want to walk through the CSV together. If you want, Alex can circulate a minimal SOW for signature and we can start provisioning once it's signed.
